q: How far does the bike move per pedal turn at a ratio of 2.0?
A straight line through the origin: distance is proportional to the ratio.
Calculate the expected distance at a ratio of 3.0 and compare.
Explain why a rider chooses a ratio of 0.9 on a steep hill.
Each pedal turn moves the bike only 1.9 m, so less work per turn is needed and the pedal force is smaller: the rider can keep climbing.
